chunks: From him, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from Ja'far, from his father, that Ali (peace be upon him) said:

There is no *li'an* (mutual imprecation) between five types of women and their husbands: The Jewish woman who is under a Muslim man and he accuses her; The Christian woman; The slave woman who is under a free man and he accuses her; The free woman who is under a slave man and he accuses her; The one flogged for false accusation (because Allah the Exalted says 'And do not accept their testimony ever'); And the mute woman, for there is no *li'an* between her and her husband, for *li'an* is by the tongue.
The discussion on similar reports to this hadith has already passed, so what we said there is sufficient here, if Allah wills.

key_terms.مُلاَعَنَةٌ: Li'an: The ritual of mutual imprecation between husband and wife in case of adultery accusation.

ai.seo_question: Which five types of women are exempt from the ritual of Li'an in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) specifies five categories where *li'an* is inapplicable, highlighting that the ritual's validity hinges on the accuser's capacity for verbal declaration, thereby excluding mute women. The inclusion of *al-majlood* (the one flogged for false accusation) is grounded in the Quranic principle that their testimony is permanently rejected, rendering their accusations legally insufficient to trigger the *li'an* procedure. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the precise conditions of testimony and verbal capacity in marital dispute resolution.
